# Conservative Party Manifesto 2015: Summary

## Core Economic Vision
The Conservative Party's 2015 manifesto centers on continuing their "long-term economic plan" following the 2010 financial recovery. They claim to have halved the deficit, created 1.9 million jobs, and transformed Britain into one of the fastest-growing major economies. Their primary commitment is eliminating the deficit entirely and running a surplus by 2018-19—the first in 18 years.

## Tax and Welfare Reforms
The manifesto promises significant tax changes: raising the personal allowance to £12,500 (removing minimum wage workers from income tax entirely), increasing the 40p tax threshold to £50,000, and freezing VAT and National Insurance. They pledge a "Tax-Free Minimum Wage" enshrined in law.

Welfare reforms include reducing the benefit cap from £26,000 to £23,000, rolling out Universal Credit, and abolishing automatic Housing Benefit for 18-21 year-olds. They propose replacing Jobseeker's Allowance for young people with a time-limited Youth Allowance requiring work or training.

## Housing and Infrastructure
Housing commitments include 200,000 Starter Homes at 20% below market price for under-40s, extending Right to Buy to Housing Association tenants, and continuing Help to Buy schemes. They promise major infrastructure investment: £38 billion for railways, £15 billion for roads, and ambitious broadband expansion targeting 95% superfast coverage by 2017.

## NHS and Education
The NHS receives pledges of £8 billion additional funding by 2020, seven-day GP access, and same-day appointments for over-75s. Education promises include 500 new free schools, converting failing schools to academies, protecting per-pupil funding, and creating 3 million apprenticeships while removing university place caps.

## Europe and Immigration
The manifesto's most significant constitutional pledge is an in-out EU referendum by end of 2017, following renegotiation of Britain's membership terms. Immigration controls include requiring four years' residency before EU migrants can claim benefits, ending Housing Benefit for EU jobseekers, and maintaining the net migration target of "tens of thousands."

## Security and Constitutional Reform
Defense commitments include maintaining the Trident nuclear deterrent, keeping regular forces above 82,000, and meeting NATO's 2% GDP spending target. Domestically, they pledge to scrap the Human Rights Act, introduce English votes for English laws, and implement further Scottish and Welsh devolution following the Smith Commission recommendations.
